sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fast-Casual Self-Serve Broth Bowl Master Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic code tradition); unitary state; separate administrative court jurisdiction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 26 Nov 2007; in force 15 Oct 2010)
France–China Double Taxation Agreement (Convention of 30 Nov 1984 as amended by the Protocol of 26 Jun 2013; effective 1 Jan 2015)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 Dec 2020; ratification pending and currently suspended at EU level)
France–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1994 Convention as amended by the 2006 Protocol; effective 16 Dec 2009)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (Convention of 19 June 2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles L561-1 to L561-50 and R561-1 et seq.; Loi Sapin II No. 2016-1691 of 9 Dec 2016; Décret No. 2018-284 of 18 Apr 2018 (UBO filings); Ordonnance No. 2020-115 of 12 Feb 2020 (transposition of AMLD5, including indirect UBO control and domestic PEPs); Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L123-1 to L123-8 and R123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); French FIU is Tracfin. The UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) is submitted to the greffe du tribunal de commerce through the Guichet Unique within 30 days of incorporation; access to the register is restricted to Tracfin, supervisors, and designated obliged entities following CJEU Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 Nov 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport of each UBO and manager (KYC identity document)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC Notary Public and Exit-Entry Administration of the Ministry of Public Security of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (PRC accession in force since 7 Nov 2023) plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (criminal record extract) for each manager and UBO, equivalent to French bulletin n°2
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate existence of any intervening corporate shareholder or franchise parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Financial capacity certificate / capital availability confirmation (attestation de fonds disponibles) in substitution for the abolished blocked capital deposit for SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for French-issued bank letters; foreign bank references notarized and apostilled

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the local incorporation agent / avocat, if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and sworn French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under Articles L561-10 and L562-1 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code. All shareholders above the 25% UBO threshold, the SAS president, signatories, and the franchise operator must be screened against: (i) TRACFIN national AML/CFT guidelines and red-flag indicators for restaurant/cash-intensive businesses; (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (Regulations (EC) No 2580/2001 and (EU) No 269/2014); (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated list; (iv) French asset-freezing decisions of the Direction Générale du Trésor; and (v) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists as cross-border best practice. Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for any domestic or foreign PEP, including Chinese PEPs, and for persons connected to high-risk third countries. False UBO declarations trigger criminal liability under Articles L574-1 and L574-4 of the Monetary and Financial Code and constitute grounds for refusal of registration by the greffe.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI; public search and verification via Infogreffe.fr and INPI Data (trademark and company-name search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory language for all statutory documents and contracts under the Toubon Law No. 94-665 of 4 Aug 1994. The statutory company name (dénomination sociale) must be expressed in Latin script; a purely ideographic Chinese name is not acceptable for RCS registration. The statutory name should therefore combine a romanized/French transliteration of the brand (e.g., 'MALATANG PARIS SAS') while the commercial sign (enseigne) may display Chinese characters in marketing material. Statutory documents must state the corporate name, the legal form 'SAS', the share capital, and the RCS number.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK and any banking vocabulary (reserved to ACPR-authorized credit institutions)
MUTUELLE (reserved to specific mutual insurance forms)
RÉPUBLIQUE, FRANCE, PRÉFECTURE, MINISTÈRE, OFFICIEL, NATIONAL (impermissible connotations of public authority under Article R123-53 of the Commercial Code)
AVOCAT, NOTAIRE, PHARMACIE, MÉDECIN and other regulated professional titles
FIDUCIE (trust-like activities subject to Articles 2011 et seq. of the Civil Code)
CRÉDIT, CAISSE D'ÉPARGNE (reserved banking terminology requiring prior regulatory authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a motivated refusal by the Guichet Unique operator (INPI) or the greffe, the applicant may first file a correction/re-examination request through the portal within one month. In parallel, the applicant may petition the juge commis à la surveillance du registre at the competent tribunal de commerce within 8 days of the refusal, requesting a registration order based on the Commercial Code name-clearance rules; the court order, if favorable, is resubmitted to the greffe. An adverse order may be appealed to the commercial chamber of the cour d'appel within 15 days, followed by a pourvoi en cassation limited to points of law. In practice, most name rejections are resolved by a revision of the proposed name rather than litigation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted in principle under the statutory domiciliation regime (Articles L123-11-1 and L123-11-2 of the Commercial Code) through an approved domiciliation provider, provided the provider is registered with the regional prefect. For a fast-casual self-serve food franchise, the restaurant operating premises must nevertheless be physical and equipped for food preparation from day one, with a formal Déclaration d'activité under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and procedural registration of the establishment; a purely paper SAS with no real kitchen or staff would be red-flagged by Tracfin and would fail the franchisor's substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH for the operating restaurant: approximately 85% probability of unannounced inspection by the Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) within the first 12 months, owing to Regulation (EU) 2017/625 official food-control rules. MODERATE for the registered office: approximately 20% probability of a substance check by Tracfin, URSSAF, or the greffe in the first year, especially when using a domiciliation service; low (~5%) for random DGCCRF market-surveillance visits concerning franchise disclosure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of bilingual (FR/EN) SAS statuts with governance, share-transfer, and non-competition clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Avocat admitted to the Paris Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee; prevailing Paris market benchmark (EUR 1,000–1,500)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS regime), and Articles R.123-1 et seq. (company registry requirements)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via Guichet Unique operated by INPI
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) and formulaire M0 (demande d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; the Articles determine the amount. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and deposited into a blocked account with a French bank or a notary (Caisse des dépôts et consignations) until registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders hereby adopt the Articles of Association of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS), subscribe to the initial share capital in full, and fix the registered office at the premises indicated in Article 4 of the Articles; RESOLVED, that [President Name] be appointed as President, with sole power to represent the company, to open a corporate bank account, deposit share capital, and execute all incorporation and registration instruments; RESOLVED, that the President shall approve the legal notice, sign the M0 form, and submit the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; RESOLVED, that all officers accept their appointments and act as good managers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signature of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if real estate contribution) or shareholders themselves
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, specifying the SAS legal form, corporate purpose (including fast-casual self-serve Malatang restaurant), share capital and division, registered office address, duration, and internal management rules. If a real property lease or contribution is involved, notarization is mandatory; otherwise, execute as a private deed. Ensure the President is named and the capital contributions are listed.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of shareholders and President
Draft Articles of Association in French
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of registry query, amend and re-sign the affected clauses; notarial defects may be cured by a rectification deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or notary (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked corporate account in the name of the SAS in formation. Transfer the cash contributions via wire from shareholders. Obtain the blocking certificate (certificat du dépositaire) confirming the deposit amount and subscriber details. This certificate is required for the registration application.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening documentation (ID, KYC, corporate purpose)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC, supply updated beneficial ownership declarations. If the capital is insufficient, request additional subscriptions and reissue the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legally authorized Journal d'annonces légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit a mandatory legal notice containing the company name, legal form (SAS), capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and identification of the President (and statutory auditor, if any). After publication, obtain the attestation de parution.
required_dossiers: Final version of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publisher rejects the notice for incomplete information, correct and republish; obtain a fresh attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application via Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Guichet unique des formalités
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the official portal (procedures.inpi.fr), complete the M0 form for an SAS, and pay the administrative fee. Upload the Articles, deposit certificate, legal announcement attestation, proof of domiciliation, identity documents, and a declaration of no criminal record for the legal representatives. Submit and track the application.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Association
Attestation de parution of legal notice
Proof of domiciliation (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Copy of IDs and address proof of legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a rejection, correct the constituent deficiencies and resubmit within 30 days. An appeal can be made to the Greffe within one month of a final refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities and Issue of Extrait Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the Extrait Kbis (official company certificate). This formally constitutes the SAS. Subsequently, complete social registration with URSSAF, open a transactional corporate bank account (if not already done), and register for VAT with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed, request an interim certificate from the Greffe. Correct any erroneous social or tax registrations by online rectification requests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – simplified registration; no full EIA required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must be pretreated with a grease separator (NF EN 858-1), pH must remain between 5.5 and 8.5, suspended solids below 1,000 mg/L; cooking fumes must comply with local atmospheric discharge thresholds (VOCs and odors) as defined by the municipal sanitation code and prefectural order; solid waste disposal through licensed commercial collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance notification (attestation de conformité incendie) issued by the local Commission de Sécurité; structural load assessment for kitchen equipment; workplace health and safety clearance per the French Labor Code (Code du travail); mandatory food hygiene training (HACCP) for the responsible manager; employee occupational health visits (visite initiale) with the occupational physician.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), acting through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Business formation and corporate registration information is filed through the mandatory one-stop shop operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must submit its incorporation and beneficial-owner information through the INPI one-stop shop. The filing is transmitted to the competent registries and tax administration. The entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity, a SIRET number for each establishment, and an APE activity code. The DGFiP then assigns the French intra-Community VAT identification number, generally composed of the country prefix FR, a two-character control key, and the nine-digit SIREN number. The entity must provide constitutional documents, registered-office evidence, identification of legal representatives, beneficial-owner information, business activity details, bank information where requested, and evidence supporting the effective commencement of taxable activities. A foreign entity with no French establishment that carries out transactions requiring French VAT registration must apply to the competent non-established-business tax service of the DGFiP. A non-EU business may generally be required to appoint an accredited French tax representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement removes that requirement. VAT registration is not itself a substitute for customs registration; an EORI number is required for customs operations involving imports or exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is subject to French corporate income tax by default. It may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime if statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying size, ownership, management, activity, and age requirements; the election is generally limited to five financial years and must be notified within the applicable statutory period. The election is not a United States-style check-the-box election. France has no general elective hybrid classification mechanism for a SAS. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive provisions and may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief for arrangements involving hybrid instruments or entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), integrated with the European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French business, VAT registration is generally required from the commencement of taxable transactions unless the business qualifies for the domestic VAT exemption for small businesses (franchise en base de TVA). The principal franchise threshold for services and mixed activities is generally EUR 37,500 of annual turnover, with a tolerance threshold generally around EUR 41,250, subject to the applicable financial year and legislative amendments. A restaurant business exceeding the applicable threshold, opting voluntarily for VAT, or undertaking transactions requiring a VAT number must register. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold may apply to specified cross-border B2C digital, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services; it is not the ordinary threshold for an establishment-based French restaurant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for all domestic transactions. French businesses must issue invoices containing mandatory legal particulars and retain them in an auditable form. Domestic B2B e-invoicing and transaction reporting are being phased in under the French reform: all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and medium-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026, while small and micro-enterprises generally become subject to issuance from 1 September 2027. B2C and certain cross-border transaction data will be reported electronically under the e-reporting rules. Invoices will generally be transmitted through an approved private platform or the public invoicing portal under the final implementation framework. Digital signatures, qualified electronic seals, electronic data interchange, or documented audit-trail controls may be used to establish authenticity, integrity, and legibility. Restaurant point-of-sale systems must support compliant receipts, accounting records, and VAT evidence; there is no general French requirement for a separate real-time fiscal stamp on every receipt.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT if the seller is the exporter or can substantiate the export through customs records and transport evidence. Goods supplied to a customer in another EU Member State may qualify as an exempt intra-Community supply only where the statutory conditions are met, including customer VAT identification, dispatch to another Member State, accurate recapitulative reporting, and proof of transport. Services are not generally treated as exported goods. B2B services supplied to a customer established outside France are ordinarily taxed according to the applicable place-of-supply rule, often with no French VAT where the customer is established outside France, provided the customer status and contractual performance evidence are substantiated. Restaurant and catering services are generally taxed where physically performed, so services physically provided in France ordinarily remain subject to French VAT. Export exemption or non-taxation must be supported contemporaneously; unsupported claims may result in VAT assessment, denial of input-tax recovery, interest, and penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU customs export declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and electronic customs exit confirmation
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and applicable VAT treatment
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or equivalent evidence of dispatch outside the European Union
Proof of delivery or destination outside the European Union where the customs exit record does not independently establish the complete export chain
Contract, purchase order, packing list, and inventory records linking the exported goods to the customs declaration
Evidence of the customer's identity and place of establishment where an intra-Community supply or cross-border service rule is relied upon
French VAT account records, VAT return support, and recapitulative statements or customs data required for the relevant transaction
Inward remittance certificate: not a standard French statutory export-VAT document; bank payment evidence may be retained as corroborative commercial evidence but does not replace customs exit proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export-VAT exemption requires reliable customs, transport, contractual, and accounting evidence. The DGFiP and customs authorities may deny or claw back the exemption and assess the underlying VAT, applicable late-payment interest, and penalties. A deliberate tax breach may attract a penalty of up to 40 percent of the reassessed tax; fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights may attract up to 80 percent. Failure to provide documents, inaccurate invoices, omitted reporting, or unsupported input-VAT recovery may trigger additional penalties under the applicable Tax Code provisions. Fraudulent VAT refund claims or organized VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure, including fines and imprisonment, in addition to repayment of the improperly obtained refund and accessories.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank, executing ESCB monetary policy) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, acting as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Ministry of Economy and Finance) for external financial regulations, together with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a fully liberalised jurisdiction for both current and capital account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier). The euro is fully convertible; there are no exchange-control approvals for current-account payments, dividends, royalty remittances, or capital movements. Profit remittance from the French SAS is unrestricted in law, subject only to standard corporate formalities (audited accounts where applicable, shareholder approval of dividends, or contractual royalty documentation) and to mandatory statistical reporting to the Banque de France for the balance of payments. Non-resident shareholders may freely receive dividends; no special profit-transfer authorisation is required. The only constraints are general EU/UN/OFAC sanctions compliance and the obligation to declare cross-border transactions exceeding regulatory thresholds for balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France imposes no surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion obligation on export or trade receivables. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts with authorised banks without any statutory conversion ratio. However, the Banque de France requires a monthly 'external trade declaration' (declaration des échanges de biens) for goods exports and a 'declaration de transfert de fonds' for all cross-border monetary flows (transfers between residents and non-residents) exceeding €25,000 per transaction or aggregation, for statistical purposes only; this does not constitute a surrender or conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB / Crédit Agricole Regional Banks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High for licensed EU/UK EMIs; Low for offshore or unregulated digital payment providers. Under the French transposition of PSD2, a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) with a full EEA passport can lawfully provide payment accounts, currency conversion, and cross-border transfers to the French SAS without a banking licence. French-licensed neobanks (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Lydia Solutions) and major EEA EMIs (e.g., Ebury, WorldFirst) are viable for operational treasury, royalty collections via virtual IBANs, and supplier disbursements. However, a capital escrow account for substantiating share capital and receiving inbound FDI should be held at a full credit institution, not an EMI, given the stricter repayment-guarantee and segregation constraints under French banking law. Offshore EMIs without an ACPR licence or EEA passport cannot provide regulated payment services from within France and may not be used as the primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SAS legal representative (director) is the default and most robust onboarding route under French AML/KYC practice (Articles L561-5 et seq., Code Monétaire et Financier). French banks apply reinforced due diligence to non-resident directors and foreign beneficial owners, and a physical interview at the bank's French branch is generally required to satisfy internal compliance and to open a corporate account with full transactional authority. Remote opening is possible but only where the bank accepts the AMF-sanctioned video-identity verification (video-e-signature) process and where the director's identity documents and corporate authorisations can be certified by a French notary or a consular/embassy apostille. In practice, for a Stage-4 corporate account requiring inbound capital and active cross-border flows, a physical appearance by the SAS président at a Paris/Lyon branch — or the prior delivery of a notarised delegation of signature to a French-resident authorised signatory — is strongly recommended and materially increases onboarding velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP exposure, and adverse media screening of non-resident beneficial owners and of the Chinese shareholder/franchisor group
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of passports and valid residence permits of all UBOs; an org chart identifying all shareholders above 25%; an EU/OFAC/UN sanctions clearance certificate produced by a reputable third-party screening provider; a notarial certificate of identity and address; a sworn declaration of funds provenance; group corporate registration extracts (Chinese business licence) with apostille and official translation; and written confirmation that no UBO is a politically exposed person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth for the inbound capital injection (initial share capital and shareholder loans)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the remitting shareholder's bank evidencing lawful accumulation of funds; a signed share subscription agreement and board/shareholder resolution authorising the remittance; the French SAS bank certificate of deposit or escrow confirmation; corporate tax certificates for the shareholder entity proving tax standing; and, where funds include intra-group loans, a notarised shareholder loan agreement with market-rate interest and a repayment schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial logic of outbound royalty/trade flows to the Chinese franchisor or trademark owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed Master Franchise and Trademark License Agreement between the SAS and the Chinese brand owner; the international or French trademark registration certificate (INPI/CNIPA/WIPO) evidencing the licensor's title; a transfer-pricing benchmark or royalty valuation summary confirming arm's-length rates; and a projected royalty invoice template with clear calculation methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cash-turnover profile and POS-intensive operations characteristic of a fast-casual dining franchise
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented cash management and POS reconciliation policy (daily banking of card and cash takings, segregation of store floats, monthly treasury reconciliation); the certified POS/acquirer contract with a licensed French acquiring bank; accounting system audit trail (e.g., ERP or invoicing software with audit logs); and a provisional business plan with monthly revenue and cash-flow forecasts, to demonstrate low money-laundering risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remoteness of non-resident director and inability to satisfy physical-interview requirements at initial onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised power of attorney appointing a French-resident authorised signatory (or a Comité de Direction member domiciled in France); a certified copy of the director's passport and proof of address; an AMF-compliant video-identity verification report; corporate constitutive documents (statuts) with UBO declarations; and a letter from the bank's compliance officer accepting enhanced due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the initial share capital and shareholder-loan injection: (i) remit via SWIFT MT103 from the Chinese shareholder's corporate account to the SAS's capital escrow account at BNP Paribas or Société Générale; (ii) include in the MT103 narrative field the French SAS SIREN/LEI number and the purpose code stating 'Share capital subscription – apport en compte courant d'associé' or 'Capital contribution'; (iii) attach a board/shareholder resolution of the French SAS approving the capital increase and the exact remittance amount; (iv) supply the beneficiary bank with the signed share-subscription deed and, where applicable, the shareholder-loan agreement; (v) file with the Banque de France the monthly external transfer declaration (déclaration de transfert de fonds) for any amount above €25,000; (vi) comply with the French foreign-direct-investment (FDI) notification regime if the Chinese investor's sector or control threshold triggers review — restaurants and food-service operations are generally outside the strategic-sector list, but confirmation by counsel is required; (vii) verify that the sending bank's SWIFT BIC and intermediary chain pass EU/OFAC sanctions screening and that no sanctioned counterparty appears in the transaction chain.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty and trade settlements from the French SAS may be executed through: (i) SWIFT MT103 for low-value and recurring royalty payments to the Chinese franchisor, using purpose code 'IP License Fees / Royalties' and including the underlying contract reference and the SAS SIREN in the narrative; such payments settle over T2/TARGET2 and are subject to automatic overnight Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting; (ii) a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary LC, UCP 600) issued by a French bank in favour of Chinese equipment or ingredient suppliers for capital procurement (e.g., hot-pot equipment, packaging, speciality ingredients), with the confirmation typically at a Chinese bank such as Bank of China, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, or China Merchants Bank to mitigate documentary risk; payment terms under the LC are drawn at sight or usance in EUR/USD/CNY as contractually allocated; (iii) for high-frequency supplier payments, an open-account SWIFT rail authorised under the Master Franchise Agreement with monthly netting; and (iv) all disbursements must pass through the SAS's operational account with the bank's automatic reporting to the Banque de France — there is no approval requirement, but there is a mandatory €25,000 reporting threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) traded with a French/French-branch bank under ISDA/2018 French Master Agreement, eligible without EMIR clearing for Non-Financial Counterparty - (NFC-) below thresholds
FX swaps (EUR/CNY, EUR/USD) for managing near-term liquidity and rolling settlement mismatch

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on the offshore CNY (CNH) where onshore CNY convertibility is constrained; NDFs are permissible for hedging genuine commercial exposure with a licensed French counterparty, not for speculative purposes
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium-term shareholder-loan exposures, subject to EMIR reporting and, if the SAS qualifies as NFC+, mandatory clearing
European-style FX options (plain-vanilla zero-premium collars) to cap translation/transaction risk on the Chinese renminbi cash flows

All instruments must be used strictly for hedging underlying commercial contract exposures, documented through a board-approved treasury and hedging policy, and executed under MiFID II suitability requirements with the relevant French banking counterparty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Bilans, Comptes de Résultat and Annexe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the closing of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000 and risk of company administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Upon incorporation and upon any change; annual compliance review required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and potential sanctions for non-compliance with anti-money laundering rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Changes to Directors and Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for late filing and potential administrative measures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Turnover > €50 million OR balance sheet total > €43 million OR average headcount > 500 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Comptabilité Générale Applicable en France)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and confirmation of shareholding structure and UBO register; updates required for any shareholding transfers or ownership changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €38,120 of taxable profit for SMEs meeting specific ownership and revenue criteria; Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; indefinite tax loss carryforward with annual deduction capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable income exceeding that threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa No. 2065 (liasse fiscale) via EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) on impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December: file by the second business day after 1 May (typically 3 May). For any other fiscal year ending date: file by the second business day after expiry of 3 months from the closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal form, name, SIREN number, address, fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French tax identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) and note the non-resident status in the annex if required for the PE declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Activity data: ISIC/NACE code, business scope, and declaration of any permanent establishment in France.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned SAS, confirm that the French entity constitutes a permanent establishment of its parent only if significant management functions are exercised in France; otherwise state independence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable results: net profit or loss, deductions, and any tax credits (CIR, CICE) applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all cross-border transactions with related parties are reported at arm’s length; attach TP documentation if thresholds are met or if a treaty claim for reduced withholding tax is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit allocation: fixed assets, shareholders’ loans, and dividends distributed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If dividends are declared to a non-resident parent, disclose the beneficiary’s country and tax residence, and prepare Form 5000/TRC for treaty reduction from 25% to the applicable rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due if filed more than 30 days after deadline, otherwise 5%; plus late payment interest of 0.2% per month of delay; additional €150 per missing annex document after formal notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced dividend rate under the France-China DTA (2021 protocol), the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Chinese tax authority, complete Form 5000, and submit it to the French tax administration (SIE du lieu de dépôt) before the dividend payment date. The effective treaty rate is 5% when the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the capital of the French SAS, otherwise 10%. The payer must receive the TRC and file an application for reduced withholding with the dividend return (Form 2561).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 33.33%, reduced to 10% under the France-China DTA. Interest: generally no withholding tax under French domestic law for commercial interest; if the DTA applies, the maximum rate is 10%, but most commercial interest is exempt under domestic rules for non-residents unless the debt qualifies as a loan subscribed in France (case-by-case).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In EUR: â‚¬400,000,000 annual turnover (or â‚¬40,000,000 total balance sheet assets) for mandatory large enterprise documentation; simplified documentation required for turnover between â‚¬50,000,000 and â‚¬400,000,000 if the entity holds or is held by a company meeting the €50M turnover threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the OECD/G20 BEPS measures, including the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD), requiring genuine economic substance for treaty benefits and to avoid 'abus de droit'. An SAS must demonstrate actual management activity, payroll, and operational decision-making in France; absence may trigger tax residency reclassification or denial of treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, concealment of bank accounts, failure to issue invoices for franchise royalties and service fees, or use of fictitious expense deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, plus late payment interest; criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for corporate officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for the full tax debt if they committed 'faute de gestion' or acted in bad faith; travel bans and criminal imprisonment may be imposed. The corporate veil can be pierced for fictitious or fraudulent inter-company transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling franchise services or charging royalties at undervalued rates to a related Chinese entity, or failing to provide contemporaneous TP documentation when above thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income at arm’s length, penalty of 5% of the reassessed amount (or 10% if no documentation), plus interest at 0.2% monthly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and legal representative may be ordered to pay the additional tax if they controlled the pricing decisions and knowingly departed from correct transfer pricing rules, leading to a judicial conviction for 'abus de biens sociaux'.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS solely to benefit from the China-France tax treaty without any real commercial activity, employees, or physical premises in France; using a mailbox address as the registered office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, immediate application of the 25% dividend withholding tax without reduction; fines up to €50,000 for failure to meet substance guidelines; reinstatement of tax under anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for the difference between the treaty rate and statutory rate if they certified false statements; criminal penalties for misuse of corporate assets may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a beneficial owner with the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS) or failure to implement AML controls for franchise partners and licensees, particularly when using local POS and cross-border royalty wires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million per violation for SARL/SAS entities; non-compliance with beneficial ownership reporting can result in €5,000 to €25,000 penalties for the legal entity and directors separately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal liability for 'blanchiment' (money laundering) if directors deliberately circumvent AML controls to facilitate franchisee fraud; imprisonment up to 5 years and personal asset forfeiture.
